key_insight: Vine Codes are quantum LDPC codes that achieve lower qubit overhead than surface codes while remaining implementable on a planar square grid using only nearest-neighbour superconducting gates.
engineering_relevance: They offer a practical path to more hardware-efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation on superconducting platforms without requiring long-range connectivity.
method: Generalize Directional Codes to open-boundary planar layouts using routing qubits
Search numerically for low-overhead candidate codes and verify circuit distances
Evaluate performance with circuit-level noise simulations under realistic superconducting error rates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports candidate codes such as [[121,4,6]], [[221,6,7]], and [[234,9,6]], with up to ~28% fewer data/measure qubits at circuit distance 7 and ~18% fewer total qubits at distance 10, plus better-than-surface-code performance at noise rate 10^-3.
watch_item: The approach still depends on added routing qubits and careful layout/circuit synthesis, so hardware implementation complexity may limit near-term gains.
paper_title: Vine Codes: Low-Overhead Quantum LDPC Codes on a Planar Square Grid
